name: NexiGo Aurora Pro
description: Runs on the NexiGo Aurora Pro projector's own Android and puts the projector on this kiosk's Home Assistant device: a Picture switch that blanks the laser the way the projector's power menu does (fans stop, Android stays awake, back in a second), Input and Picture mode selects, laser hours and light-engine temperatures, and buttons that open the projector's settings app (keystone, focus) and drive the front LED bar. Uses the vendor's projector-test tool and system properties; no root. Shizuku is optional and only adds the temperature readings.
author: David Coulson

settings.title: Read the projector every
settings.description: How often the plugin reads the light, input, picture mode, laser hours and temperatures back from the projector.

settings.title: Stay on when the source sleeps
settings.description: Keeps the projector on the network around the clock: ignores the CEC standby a sleeping Apple TV or console broadcasts and turns off the no-signal shutdown. Pair it with an automation that turns Picture off when the source sleeps. Turning this off does not restore the projector's own settings.

settings.title: Front LEDs follow the picture
settings.description: The front bar shows the projector's standby lights while the picture is off and goes dark while it shows - whether the picture was changed here, by a remote key or by the projector's own menu. The Front LEDs select still sets any pattern by hand.

settings.title: Run commands through
settings.description: Auto tries the kiosk process itself first (works on the stock firmware, whose SELinux is permissive), then the projector's own ADB daemon over the loopback address (port 5555 is open with no key on the stock firmware, and it is there after every reboot), then Shizuku. Behind a direct channel the log, and so the temperatures, come through ADB or Shizuku.

settings.title: Start Shizuku after a reboot
settings.description: When Shizuku is installed and not running, start it through the loopback ADB session at every plugin start, so the other plugins that want it (Network ADB, Device Performance) have it back without anyone touching the projector or Home Assistant.
